title: Reduce CI noise and latency by introducing layered builder profiles and smart remote-cache eviction
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: our CI has grown noisy and slow due to fat base images, repeated language/toolchain installs, and an undifferentiated caching strategy. This causes longer PR feedback loops and increased cost.

Goal: shrink CI runtime and variance by defining layered builder profiles (minimal base, language runtime layers, and ephemeral build-time tooling), adopting BuildKit+CAS where helpful, and implementing a smart remote-cache eviction policy to keep hot layers available while pruning low-value artifacts. Also split lint/tooling into fast-path runners to reduce feedback latency for fast PRs.

Non-goals: full monorepo refactor or changing runtime production images (this ticket focuses on builder images and CI ergonomics).

Deliverables:
- layered builder images (base-runtime, language-runners: node, go, rust, python; tooling shim) with clear version pins and smaller attack surface
- migration scripts and templates for Dockerfiles that target the layered profiles
- remote CAS eviction policy implemented in the cache proxy (LRU with TTL tiers + size caps) and dashboards to show hit/miss and eviction churn
- move lint/typecheck/format quick-runners to separate lightweight jobs that run pre-merge; gate long builds to main pipeline
- toolchain upgrade plan (Node 20.x, Go 1.21, Rust 1.73) with compatibility checklist and targeted migration PRs

Success criteria:
- median CI runtime for common PRs reduced by >=25%
- cache hit rate for primary build artifacts >=90% for active branches
- CI cost per commit reduced by >=15% over baseline

Risks & trade-offs:
- Splitting images increases complexity in Dockerfile authoring — mitigated by templates and generator scripts.
- Aggressive eviction could cause cache thrash for bursts — start conservative, observe metrics, then tune.
- Toolchain upgrades may surface flaky tests; we will run upgrade branches and use staged rollout in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Layered builder images published to internal registry and referenced by example repos
Remote cache proxy supports TTL tiers and reports eviction metrics
Lint quick-run jobs added to default PR workflow and pass on >95% of recent PRs
Toolchain upgrade PRs merged for node/go/rust with test matrix green on dedicated runners
rollout_plan: Week 1: publish layered image specs and update internal Dockerfile templates
Week 2: enable builder profiles on ~20 active repos as canary, monitor cache hit/eviction
Week 3: deploy smart eviction policy (conservative thresholds) to cache proxy; measure churn
Week 4: flip default workflow to use lint quick-run; continue repo migrations and tune eviction
Week 5: widen rollout to org-wide and finalize toolchain upgrade merges
metrics: Median CI wall-clock time (baseline vs current): target -25%
Cache hit ratio for build layers: target >=90%
Remote cache eviction rate: target <5% per hour on stable periods

2025-02-24 - SRE: Reviewed eviction approach. Recommended starting with TTL tiers (1h / 12h / 72h) + size cap per tenant, avoid global LRU for cost-accounting reasons. Will add metrics to Grafana dashboard.

2025-03-02 - Engineering Manager (Liam O'Connor): Approved increasing estimate by 2 points to allow for cross-repo migrations and additional test flakiness fixes. Noted dependency on ENG-61421 for build template rollout coordination.
